title: thread-prioritization-and-historical-compression-prd-scratch
content:
TL;DR: Sketching a feature that treats conversation history as a first-class resource: automated historical compression + per-message prioritization that tells the serving runtime what to keep, what to compress (summarize), and what to drop. Goal: reduce tokens sent to model without losing user-visible quality; give product teams fine-grained controls for latency/cost/quality tradeoffs.

Why now / motivation
- Hosted customers are hitting token cost and latency spikes for long multi-turn flows (support bots, tutoring, docs assistants).
- We have caching + prefix pruning today but it’s coarse: caches by prefix exactly, and session store UX is manual.
- If we can automatically summarize low-value history and mark high-value context, we reduce per-request cost and surface clear controls for teams.
- Differentiator: expose prioritization metadata to runtime (dedicated/private) so routing/caching/quantization decisions can be context-aware.

High-level idea
- Two parts: (A) Historical Compression — automated summarizers that generate compact representations of older turns (configurable cadence + fidelity). (B) Priority Markers — an API/SDK flag per user message or intent that marks it as HIGH/MED/LOW importance for retention in context or in cache.
- Runtime uses these markers to decide kv-cache retention, batching/eviction, and whether to call a summarizer before sending tokens.

User stories
- As a product engineer, I want conversation history older than N turns to be auto-compressed into a 1–3 sentence summary so my token costs don’t grow indefinitely.
- As an SRE, I want long-tail requests to degrade gracefully: older low-priority turns get summarized or omitted under load to maintain latency SLOs.
- As a PM for a tutoring product, I want to mark solution messages as HIGH priority so they’re always in context; filler chit-chat can be compressed to preserve continuity but not verbatim text.

API sketch (surface-level)
- Sessions.create or messages.send accepts optional metadata: {priority: "high|med|low", compress: "auto|never|always", tags: ["exam-step","answer"]}
- New endpoint: sessions.summarize(session_id, until_turn=42, level="concise|detailed") -> returns compressed text stored in session store and referenced by runtime via pointer
- Console: per-session timeline view that shows which turns were compressed + ability to expand/restore verbatim for debugging

Console / UX
- New tab in session viewer: Compression timeline. Color-coded markers (green=high priority, amber=med, grey=low/compressed).
- Quick toggle: Experiment mode where product teams can preview the compressed context used for a sample set of prompts (useful for evals).
- Rolling revert: one-click restore of last 24 hours verbatim for incident debugging (auditing considerations!).

Runtime integration notes
- We need a pre-send pipeline step: given session pointer + incoming message, expand the compressed summary up to allowed tokens; prefer preserving HIGH priority items verbatim, compress lower priority.
- For dedicated/private: provide a summarizer model bundle (small distilled model) that can run on dedicated GPUs or even CPU for private deploys. Option to disable summarizer if customer wants full verbatim.
- Cache keys should include a compression-version tag so changes to compression algorithm don’t silently break behavior.

Acceptance criteria / metrics
- Metric: 30–60% reduction in tokens/turn for long-running sessions (50+ turns) with <5% drop in key task success metric (e.g., answer correctness, user satisfaction score) on a representative eval set.
- Latency: median p50 token-send + model time should not increase >5% for typical sessions; p95 should improve under high concurrency because of lower token counts.
- Cost: estimate monthly savings for a 1M-turn customer; show ROI vs. engineering/setup time.

Quick experiments (MVP)
1) Offline eval: run an extract from 10k long sessions, apply simple heuristics (keep last 5 turns verbatim, summarize blocks of 5 older turns using gpt-small) and measure token reduction + quality delta on label tasks. Track failures where summaries drop critical info.
2) In-prod dark-launch: run summarizer but do not change tokens sent; log differences between expanded compressed context vs. gold context. Use asloss model to predict user-visible regressions.
3) Beta: opt-in beta on hosted for accounts that opt to try; provide dashboard and allow manual priority flags via SDK.

Privacy & compliance notes
- Summaries are derived data but still user content; ensure retention policies mirror verbatim retention.
- For Private(VPC/on-prem) customers, offer an offline summarizer binary (no data leaves customer infra).

Open questions / risks
- How to evaluate "importance" robustly? We can offer heuristics (message length, role=user/assistant, presence of code blocks, explicit priority flag) and ML-based importance models trained from labels. Need dataset.
- Risk of summarizer hallucination removing critical facts -> need strict hallucination detection or boil-down that prefers extraction over abstraction for certain types (code, credentials, step-by-step instructions).
- UX complexity: exposing too many knobs will confuse customers; default sensible settings and a small set of toggles is important.

Rollout plan (phases)
- Phase 0: offline eval + internal hackweek prototype (2–4 weeks)
- Phase 1: internal dark launch + console visualization (6 weeks)
- Phase 2: public beta (opt-in) with metrics dashboard and priority SDK (8–12 weeks)
- Phase 3: GA with enterprise settings (audit logs, KMS integration, versioned compression algorithms)

Implementation TODOs (notes to self)
- Collect labeled dataset for importance: ask Solutions Eng + CS for 500 sessions with hand-labeled important turns.
- Prototype summarizer using distil-xxx; prefer extractive baseline.
- Add priority metadata to SDKs (JS/Python) and backend schema (session metadata).
- Add timeline visualization wireframe to Console team backlog.

Related tickets / leads to ping
- GH#6732 (proto summarizer) - touch base with Alex R.
- CONV-4123 - dataset request from Support (Samira?)
- Slack thread: /team/product/thread-priority (context, early feedback)

Notes to self (raw)
- Keep default conservative: summarize only >30 turns or >10k tokens per session.
- Disallow compression for messages with tag: "no-compress" (ex: legal text).
- Add telemetry to show "restores" (how often teams expand compressed blocks) — if high, we’re breaking UX.

If this lands, it ties nicely to: caching (prefix + summary pointers), routing (route high-priority to low-latency pools), and optimize suggestions (we can recommend compression for cost-heavy workloads).

Questions for design review:
- Minimal API surface? prefer session-level config + per-message override.
- How transparent should summarization be to end-users? (some customers will want explicit "This conversation has been summarized" message)

End of sketch. Will refine after dataset availability check and a quick proto run.
